title: Let's take a look at Ronin (solo RPG) and talk about Dagger of Kamui (1985; Dir: Rintaro)
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ptv9GRoEKs0

Daniel (@dungeondive) pairs a samurai solo RPG with a film to watch alongside it.

**Ronin**, from Brazilian publisher Coisinha Verde, casts you as a wanderer seeking redemption — or revenge — across a fictionalised Sengoku-era Japan. Your ronin has just three stats: **reputation** (draws the villains to you), **compassion** (lost each time you kill a beaten foe, needed to charm allies) and **determination** (spent on re-rolls). Combat is a single opposed roll with no hit points; block points force re-rolls, and a loss means a d6 for death or a wound. Daniel's blind, tonfa-wielding Riku Shin wins through on blocks alone. Two lesser villains then a final boss arrive as your reputation grows, and a redemption table settles the ending. The translation is a little rough and one rules page sits oddly, but Daniel finds it fast and fun, rewarding as much journaling as you care to add.

**The Dagger of Kamui** (1985), directed by Rintaro for Madhouse, is a two-hour martial arts epic that roams from Japan to Russia to the American West — complete with cowboys and Mark Twain. Cut to 90 minutes for US VHS as *Revenge of the Ninja Warrior*, it sounds to Daniel like Leone, Kurosawa and Jodorowsky making anime together, scored with prog rock and chanting. He ranks it an underrated masterpiece, hard as it is to find.

----

What film, book or show do you pair with a solo game to get into its headspace — and has a game ever sent you hunting for one?
